what_it_does: Many modern AI models — including graph neural networks that reason over social or molecular graphs, 3-D convolution models that process point clouds, and mixture-of-experts models (large AI models that route each input to a small specialist sub-network) — all share a common three-step pattern: gather relevant data rows from scattered memory locations, multiply matrices together (the core math of neural networks), then scatter results back out. This gather-matmul-scatter pattern is irregular and hard to optimize because which rows to gather changes with every input. Efficient-GMS introduces a framework that analyzes the data flow across these steps, finds structural patterns shared by different model types, and proposes four ways to fuse (combine) the three steps to reduce redundant memory reads and writes. A lightweight performance predictor estimates which fusion strategy will be fastest for a given input size and hardware, replacing an expensive exhaustive search.
